full_judgment:
4. That the defendant No. 19 (Government) contested the suit stating, inter alia, that the suit properties are Government khas land and though the properties were leased in favour of the plaintiffs but at the instance of the defendants the settlement Appeal No. 154 of 1981-82 was filed and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong cancelled the proposals on the basis of materials on record and settlement revision No. 73 of 1984 filed before Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong was also rejected on hearing the parties. There being provisions of appeals before the higher forums, the plaintiffs did not exhaust the same. The plaintiffs have no right, title or possession in the suit land. The suit is barred under section 76(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The property stands recorded in Khas Khatian of the Government. The suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 5. The added defendant Nos. 20-26 filed the written statements denying the case of the plaintiffs and stating, inter alia, that the suit has been filed collusively by the plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 1-15, and that the suit is not maintainable and that the defendants being Member of Kakara Mini-Bazar Bittihin Samabaya Samity are in physical possession of the suit land and that the suit has not been properly valued and that the suit lands are collusion lands from the River Matamuhuri and suncrops are produced there and that the defendants getting the land on 'eksana' basis have been in physical possession of the suit land and that the plaintiffs in collusion with the defendant Nos. 1-15 collusively tried to get the suit land settled secretly and that then the added defendants and others filed Settlement Appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong and the settlement having not been finalised and approved, their appeals were found premature and the appeals were dismissed and that after approval of the settlement cases, the petitioner and others filed settlement appeal No. 154 of 1981-42 and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong cancelled the settlement as it was found that the plaintiffs are not eligible nor the lands are fit to be settled as raiyatwari settlement as it was not fit for producing paddy and there was misrepresentation of fact as to the nature of land. The order of Additional Deputy Commissioner was affirmed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong in settlement Revision No. 136 of 1985 and an appeal before the Board of Land Administration, Dhaka by forging the judgment of the Commissioner's Court was preferred but the forgery being detected, the Board "filed" the appeal and directed to refer the matter to Anti-Corruption which is pending and that by suppression of those facts, the plaintiffs collusively filed the instant suit and that the suit itself is fraudulent and malafide as the plaintiffs with oblique motive did not implead the added defendants and that plaintiff No. 2 Ali Akbar instituted a few false criminal cases against the added defendants wherein the defendant Nos. 1-15 have been cited as witness and that the plaintiff No. 2 Ali Akbar and the defendant No. 1 Kamaluddin jointly filed objection against the added defendants regarding the suit land to the local Upazila Chairman, which ipso facto proves the unholy collusion of the plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 1-15. The defendants further stated that, in view of the orders of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong cancelling the settlements proposals in the names of the plaintiffs and since no agreement was executed between the parties, no Jamabandi Khatians being created in the names of the plaintiffs, they have no right, title or possession over the suit property nor they have any locus standi to file or maintain the suit and that the suit is liable to be dismissed having no cause of action.
